text:
sarah (Finance): Heads up — vendor X sent a credit memo today for $48,120 tied to last month's pricing experiment. It affects May hosted usage invoices and will change deferred revenue we planned to recognize this month. Need quick alignment on accounting treatment and whether we net against invoices or record as a separate contra-revenue deferral.

raj (RevOps): :eyes: I flagged this earlier — the credit is for a pricing A/B we ran that inadvertently billed customers at promo rates for 3 days. Vendor reversed charged usage; we passed through billing but need to agree a revrec pattern.

emily (Accounting): Can you drop the vendor credit memo and affected invoice IDs? I'll need to map to AR and the revenue schedule. Prefer separate contra-revenue if customers were already invoiced, otherwise adjust invoices if still open.

mike (Billing Ops): Uploaded the credit memo here: https://docs.internal/vendor-credits/VM-2026-0423.csv — affected invoices: INV-7701, INV-7720, INV-7721, INV-7735. We already applied credits to INV-7701 and INV-7720; the others were recognized in deferred schedule.

acct-bot: Automated note: GL impact preview (estimate) — decrease AR by $21,400, decrease deferred revenue by $26,720. Review required before posting.

sarah (Finance): Emily — the $26.7k was in deferred revenue for multi-month commits (we recognized 30% in month of invoice). If we apply vendor credit against those invoices, I think we should reverse the proportionate recognized revenue and adjust the deferral schedule. If we treat as contra-revenue, it affects P&L immediately. Thoughts?

emily (Accounting): I'd recommend reversing recognized revenue for the portion that related to the experiment period (so adjust revrec for those specific invoice lines). For the remaining credit tied to future service, reduce deferred revenue schedule. We'll need a JE like: 
```
Dr: Revenue recognized 26,720
Cr: Deferred revenue 26,720
Dr: Accounts receivable 21,400
Cr: Revenue/Contra-revenue 21,400
```
but I'll finalize amounts after mapping. Need approval from finance leadership on approach.

laura (CFO): Quick Q — is this recurring behavior we should bake into the revenue policy? Also want to ensure we don't create mismatch in customer invoices vs revenue recognized. For this one, emily's approach seems prudent: reverse recognized revenue for the impacted window and reclass remainder from deferred to reduce future recognition. Approve posting once Emily signs off.

raj (RevOps): Agreed. Also let's update the pricing experiment runbook so billing flags any transient promos earlier. I'll add a mandatory check before experiment deploys.

mike (Billing Ops): FYI — one of the affected invoices (INV-7735) has partial payment applied. If we reverse AR, collections will need to contact customer or automatically reapply credits. I'll coordinate with collections.

emily (Accounting): I'll prepare the exact JE and attach the reconciliation. Expecting to post on the 26th close window. Will ping when ready for approval.

sarah (Finance): Thanks. Can you include the split by GL and deferred schedule rows in the note? Put in the month-end folder: https://drive.internal/monthend/2026-05/adj_notes.

emily (Accounting): Will do. Posting draft JE here by EOD for laura review.

laura (CFO): Approve provisional treatment pending Emily's final numbers. If total cash impact > $50k we'll escalate to external audit pre-close.

mike (Billing Ops): Noted. I'll start customer comms templates in case collections need to reach out.

sarah (Finance): Closing the loop — thanks team. Action items: Emily to finalize JE, Mike coordinate collections, Raj update experiment runbook, Sarah will document policy change. :white_check_mark:
